domains.proposed_domain: Riemannian geometry and geometric group theory

evidence.quote: The closed smooth three-manifold $M$ defined by [eq:torus-gluing] admits no smooth Riemannian metric of nonpositive sectional curvature.

exclusions.query: No focal points on the constructed manifold
exclusions.reason: Absence of conjugate points is weaker; the stated topological curvature obstruction also excludes a metric without focal points.

evidence.quote: The fundamental group $\Gamma=\pi_1(M)$ of the closed three-manifold defined by [eq:torus-gluing] admits no proper cocompact isometric action on a nonempty proper $\operatorname{CAT}(0)$ space.

exclusions.reason: The obstruction is tied to the prescribed torus gluing and is not asserted for every graph manifold.

evidence.quote: Let $(M,g)$ be a complete smooth Riemannian manifold. If $I_{\mathbb R}(V)\geq0$ for every smooth compactly supported field along every complete unit-speed geodesic, then $g$ has no conjugate points.

exclusions.query: Finite numerical certification of all geodesics
exclusions.reason: The index criterion requires all compactly supported fields along all complete unit-speed geodesics.

hypotheses.statement: The fundamental group $\Gamma=\pi_1(M)$ of the closed three-manifold defined by [eq:torus-gluing] admits no proper cocompact isometric action on a nonempty proper $\operatorname{CAT}(0)$ space.
The manifold $M$ admits no locally $\operatorname{CAT}(0)$ length metric inducing its manifold topology.
The closed smooth three-manifold $M$ defined by [eq:torus-gluing] admits no smooth Riemannian metric of nonpositive sectional curvature.

There are constants $\delta_0>0$ and $C<\infty$, depending only on the fixed function $\chi$, such that for $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ the path [eq:cometric-path] satisfies, in the original coordinates and in either endpoint coordinate system, $$\begin{gathered} \frac19\operatorname{Id}\preceq P\preceq18\operatorname{Id}, \qquad \frac1{18}\operatorname{Id}\preceq Q\preceq9\operatorname{Id}, \qquad \|P'\|\le C\delta, \label{eq:cometric-uniform}\\ -P''\succeq0, \qquad |P'p|^2\le C\delta\,p^{\mathsf T}(-P'')p \quad\text{for every }p\in\mathbb R^2. \label{eq:cometric-domination} \end{gathered}$$ The constants do not depend on $B_1$ or $B_2$.

The integrand defining $I_J^\perp(V)$ is the index integrand of $V^\perp=V-q_VT$. Consequently, for every smooth real function $h$, $$I_J^\perp(V+hT)=I_J^\perp(V)$$ provided both fields have the finite integrals required in [eq:normal-index-definition]. This invariance holds pointwise, without any condition on $h$ at finite endpoints.

Every finite endpoint of a neck passage is transverse to the boundary torus. Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.*

1.  *The passage is the whole real line and $t$ is constant.*

2.  *The interval component $v=\dot t$ never vanishes. The passage is either a finite crossing between the two different boundary tori, or a half-infinite interval approaching an interior equilibrium height.*




3.  *After choosing the coordinates from one boundary and translating the geodesic parameter, the passage has closure $[0,L]$, begins and ends at that boundary, and has a unique turn at $s=L/2$. In these coordinates $$\begin{gathered}
     t(0)=t(L)=0,\qquad
     v(0)=-v(L)=v_0>0,\qquad t_*=t(L/2)\in(0,1),\label{eq:turn-data}\\
     t(L-s)=t(s),\qquad v(L-s)=-v(s),\qquad
     0<F'(t)\le\kappa p_1^2\quad(0\le t\le t_*),\label{eq:turn-concavity}\\
     p_1\ne0,\qquad 0<v_0^2=F(t_*)-F(0)\le\kappa p_1^2.
     \label{eq:turn-incidence}
    \end{gathered}$$*

*An interior equilibrium height $t_\infty$ in the second alternative satisfies $F(t_\infty)=1$ and $F'(t_\infty)=0$; the velocity may tend to zero there. A geodesic tangent to a boundary torus at a finite time does not enter the open neck at that time.

Let $V$ be the restriction of a smooth compactly supported field along $\gamma$ to an entire neck passage $J$. If $J=\mathbb R$, or $v$ never vanishes on $J$, or the passage is a turn contained in one end portion $0\le\tau\le1/4$, then $$I_J^\perp(V)\ge0.$$

For all sufficiently small positive $\delta$, every returning geodesic passage of the constructed neck has nonnegative perpendicular index form $I^\perp(V)$ for every smooth field $V$ along the closed passage, with no restriction on its endpoint values. A single choice of $\delta$ works for both boundary components and all unit-speed returning geodesics.

Choose $\delta>0$ to satisfy Lemma 5 and [eq:turning-delta-choice], and then choose the boundary periods as in Section 3. Let $\gamma$ be any complete unit-speed geodesic of the resulting closed manifold. For every connected component $J$ of its visit to the open neck and every smooth compactly supported field $V$ along $\gamma$, one has $$I_J^\perp(V)\ge0,\qquad I_J(V)\ge0.$$

Let $(M,g)$ be a complete smooth Riemannian manifold and let $U\subset M$ be open. Suppose that $g$ has nonpositive sectional curvature at every point of $M\setminus U$. Assume also that, for every complete unit-speed geodesic $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$, every connected component $J$ of $\gamma^{-1}(U)$, and every smooth compactly supported field $V$ along $\gamma$, the intrinsic index form satisfies $$I_J(V)\geq 0.$$ Then $I_{\mathbb R}(V)\geq0$ for every such $\gamma$ and $V$. The same conclusion follows if the passage hypothesis is given in the stronger form $I_J^\perp(V)\geq0$.
Let $(M,g)$ be a complete smooth Riemannian manifold. If $I_{\mathbb R}(V)\geq0$ for every smooth compactly supported field along every complete unit-speed geodesic, then $g$ has no conjugate points.

coverage.checked_domain: All 16 pairs epsilon,B2 from {1/4,1/2,1,2}; boundary cases include the smallest positive admitted pair and shear above unity. This is finite rational lattice coverage only.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent Fraction formulas plus exact re-check of gluing relations, lattice coordinates and oriented area; no certification of smooth metric construction or global index estimates.
